https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/lithuan.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.07.23 11:05 Lithuania’s priority is stronger strategic partnership, PM tells Polish president Source: ELTA Seimas svarsto ir tvirtina Vyriausybės programą PHOTO: Julius Kalinskas | Elta Follow Delfi on Google During a telephone conversation with Polish President Karol Nawrocki on Wednesday, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius emphasised Lithuania’s commitment to further strengthening its strategic partnership with Poland, said the prime minister’s press service. Lithuania regards Poland as an indispensable ally, a strategic partner and a neighbouring country linked by a shared history. In his conversation with President Karol Nawrocki, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevičius expressed Lithuania’s interest in deepening bilateral relations and discussed regional security, support for Ukraine and other current issues with the Polish leader. „Today, the words of Pope John Paul II remain especially relevant: our nations are united by ties of neighbourliness, friendship and brotherhood. The challenges we face together oblige us to work jointly for the security and prosperity of our region, while our shared history reminds us that this is not only possible – it is precisely what we should strive for. Further strengthening our strategic partnership with Poland is a central objective of my Government,“ said Prime Minister Sinkevičius. The discussion focused primarily on security and defence issues. In the bilateral agenda, the Government will devote particular attention not only to this area but also to the resilience of energy and other critical infrastructure, transport and military mobility projects, economic ties – which are already strong but have further potential for growth – and cultural exchanges. The prime minister noted that, as Russia continues its military aggression against Ukraine and remains a threat to the security of Europe as a whole, it is essential to maintain active support for Ukraine and increase pressure on Russia. Mr Sinkevičius also stressed the importance of close coordination between the two countries in responding to both conventional and hybrid threats, as well as the importance of strong transatlantic relations. https://www.romania-insider.com/romania-.text: Macro Romania risks RRF funds after lawmakers delay coal plant closures 05 August 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? Share it with your friends! Facebook Twitter Google Pinterest Reddit Email LinkedIn Romania’s Parliament has moved to delay the closure of coal-fired power plants by making shutdowns conditional on replacement generation capacity being commissioned, raising the risk of a breach of commitments under the European Union’s Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF). The Senate adopted the amendments on August 4, with support from the opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD) and the far-right Alliance for the Unity of Romanians (AUR). Minister of investments and European projects Dragos Pislaru warned that the move could trigger penalties and put billions of euros in EU funding at risk. President Nicusor Dan said he would use his constitutional powers to prevent the amendments from being promulgated if they conflict with Romania’s commitments under the RRF. “If the Parliament adopts the law in the form approved by the expert committee, I will analyse it with maximum responsibility, and I will use all constitutional prerogatives, including the request for a reconsideration, so that Romania can submit the pending payment demands and not lose billions of euros under the Resilience Facility,” Dan said in a Facebook post following the Senate vote. Dispute over decarbonisation milestone Pislaru said the Senate amendments would effectively reverse a decarbonisation milestone under Romania’s National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) that has already been validated by the European Commission and linked to grants already disbursed. “We risk the total blockage of the PNRR and the loss of billions of euros in European funds,” Pislaru said, calling the move “an extremely dangerous decision”, according to B1 TV . The legislation requires coal-fired power plants to remain operational until replacement generation capacity is available. The measure is intended to prevent the loss of generating capacity before alternative sources are commissioned, but conflicts with Romania’s previously agreed timetable for coal phase-out under the PNRR. The Chamber of Deputies initially tacitly approved the initiative on May 11. The Senate’s legislative brief identified the upper house as the decision-making chamber, meaning its August 4 vote would normally have completed the parliamentary procedure. However, the legislation was placed back on the Chamber of Deputies’ agenda for August 5 after the two chambers approved different versions. The dispute leaves the measure facing further parliamentary scrutiny as Romania seeks to preserve access to RRF funding. iulian@romania-insider.com (Photo source: Cateyeperspective/Dreamstime.com ) Read next 29 July 2026 Politics Romanian Parliament passes SAFE, PNRR-related bills during extraordinary session Normal Macro Romania risks RRF funds after lawmakers delay coal plant closures 05 August 2026 Iulian Ernst Like this article? https://www.torahmusings.com/2026/08/can.text: by R. Gil Student I. Undistinguished Fathers A chazzan who leads the synagogue services represents the community before God, so halakhah asks more of him than a good voice. Ideally he should be righteous, humble, acceptable to the congregation, well versed in Torah, in addition to having a good voice ( Shulchan Arukh , Orach Chaim 53:4). However, his family background is also important. If a man is personally righteous but comes from a non-religious home, this might have bearing. Rashi (Gen. 25:21) asks why Yitzchak’s prayer for Rivkah’s infertility was accepted more than Rivkah’s own prayers. He quotes the Gemara ( Yevamos 64a) that the prayer of a tzadik ben tzadik , a two-generational righteous person, is stronger than that of a tzadik ben rasha, a first-generational righteous person. Therefore, Yitzchak ben Avraham’s prayer was accepted over Rivkah bas Besuel’s. If so, perhaps a community should prefer a chazzan whose father is righteous over a ba’al teshuvah , someone who was not raised observant. Setting aside the issue of past personal behavior, is there a concern over the ba’al teshuvah ’s father? Rav Asher ben Yechiel (Rosh; 14th cen., Germany-Spain) was asked about communities in Spain that appointed chazzanim from undistinguished families. The Rosh dismisses this concern. What good is distinguished lineage, he asks, if the man himself is wicked? And if someone comes from an undistinguished family but is righteous, all the better, since it is a mitzvah to draw close those who come from afar ( Responsa 4:22). His son, Rav Ya’akov, quotes this ruling in his important work, the Tur ( Orach Chaim 53). But it leaves open the question whether the same logic applies when the chazzan ‘s father was not only undistinguished but unobservant? Later authorities are divided on this point. II. Unobservant Fathers Rav Yoel Sirkes (Bach; 17th cen., Poland) cites Rav Shlomo Luria (Maharshal; 16th cen., Poland) as adding a qualification. Someone with an undistinguished father is acceptable but when two candidates are otherwise equal, the one whose father is righteous should be preferred ( Bach , Orach Chaim 53, s.v. ve-kasav Maharshal ). Rav Avraham Gombiner (17th cen., Poland) follows this approach and writes that it is proper to look for a chazzan who is himself the son of a righteous man ( Magen Avraham , Orach Chaim 53:8). Rav Yisrael Kagan (Chafetz Chaim; 20th cen., Poland) rules likewise ( Mishnah Berurah 53:13). Rav David Segal (17th cen., Poland) makes the Rosh’s logic more explicit. He notes that the Rosh does not merely tolerate a candidate from an undistinguished family; he says it is good to draw close those who come from afar. In other words, if there are two righteous candidates, one the son of a righteous man and the other the son of a wicked man, we should prefer the son of a wicked man ( Taz , Orach Chaim 53:3). III. Middle Ground Between the Rav Gombiner’s preference for the son of the righteous father and the Rav Segal’s preference for the righteous man who overcame a deficient family background, Rav Shneur Zalman of Liadi (early 19th cen., Russia) stakes out a middle position. He first repeats that it is good to seek a chazzan who is the son of a righteous man. He then immediately cites the other view as well, that the prayer of a righteous son of a wicked man may actually be heard more readily. In practice, he concludes, the matter depends on the relative strengths of the two candidates: one man’s humility against the other’s ancestral righteousness ( Shulchan Arukh Ha-Rav , Orach Chaim 53:7). This shifts the question away from a fixed rule about pedigree and toward a comparison of character. A religious upbringing gives someone something real: models, habits, inherited merit. Growing up without it can produce something else: humility, independence, and the achievement of having built a religious life rather than inherited one. The issue is less about who his father was than about what that background actually produced in the man standing before the congregation. More recently, Rav Moshe Sternbuch (cont., Israel) addresses this exact question. He explicitly points out something often implicit in previous discussions. There are many ways to measure the quality of a chazzan , among them his pedigree. But which qualities have higher priority than others? Rav Sternbuch argues that pedigree ranks last among them all. Only if the two candidates are equal in every other way, do we consider the righteousness of their fathers. Otherwise, we prioritize other considerations. Additionally, someone who exhibited self-sacrifice in leaving the non-religious ways of his upbringing holds a quality not found in someone who was raised religious. Moreover, it is not clear that a non-religious father who never had a proper Jewish education can be considered wicked. Rav Sternbuch concludes that if the two candidates are truly equal, the son of the righteous father should be preferred. But if the man from the non-religious home is more righteous or brings greater merit by spreading Torah, he should be chosen instead ( Teshuvos Ve-Hanhagos , vol. 4, no. 9). It is worth noting that some codes, when discussing the qualifications of a chazzan , do not mention this issue at all. Rav Ephraim Margoliyos (19th cen., Ukraine) lists the qualifications for serving as a chazzan for Selichos and the High Holidays, and does not mention pedigree ( Mateh Ephraim 581:26-28). Rav Shlomo Ganzfried (19th cen., Hungary does likewise ( Kitzur Shulchan Arukh 128:7). Rav Yitzchak Fuchs (cont., Israel) quotes the limitation of pedigree, as ruled in Mishnah Berurah , but concludes: “In practice, the one among the congregation who is greatest in wisdom and good deeds is the most appropriate one [to serve as chazzan ]” ( Tefillah Ke-Hilkhasah 26:3). While acknowledging the pedigree rule, he effectively nullifies it by lowering its priority beneath the qualifications of personal wisdom and righteousness. In this way, recent authorities acknowledge that family background and childhood training matter. However, they emphasize that what a person does with his life matters even more. https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/10/10/n.text: THE Philippine Air Force (PAF) will gain a dedicated training capability for pilots and maintenance personnel of its S-70i Black Hawk helicopters under a contract awarded to US defense contractor Lockheed Martin.The company confirmed the contract covers a full-flight simulator, a virtual maintenance trainer, instructional materials, along with spare parts and sustainment support through 2032.The system will allow PAF to conduct more local training, reducing the need for overseas facilities and operational helicopters for pilot training.The full-flight simulator will replicate the experience of flying an S-70i Black Hawk, while the virtual maintenance trainer will allow technicians to practice maintenance procedures in a simulated environment, Lockheed Martin said.The company did not disclose the contract’s value or the delivery schedule.“The PAF will continue training Black Hawk pilots at the US-based Sikorsky Training Academy while establishing its own local training capability.”The contract marks Lockheed Martin’s first order for its dedicated S-70i Black Hawk training devices, according to the company.The development comes as the Philippines continues to build its military air mobility capabilities through its fleet of Polish-made S-70i Black Hawk helicopters, manufactured at PZL Mielec, a Lockheed Martin subsidiary.The Philippines signed its first contract for 16 S-70i Black Hawks in 2019 and a second contract for 32 additional helicopters in February 2022.PZL Mielec said it completed delivery of all 48 helicopters covered by the two contracts.The S-70i Black Hawk is a multirole helicopter used for troop transport, humanitarian assistance, disaster response and other military operations.Separately, Rafal Leskiewicz, spokesman for Polish President Karol Nawrocki, said the Philippines could purchase additional Black Hawks from PZL Mielec, describing the aircraft deals as an example of economic cooperation between Poland and the Philippines.Leskiewicz said the Philippines was the largest foreign customer for Black Hawk helicopters produced at the Mielec facility and could purchase additional units.
